def: A person's recorded judgement about one item against a stated criterion, such as pass or fail.
A person who assigns labels to items by following a guideline.
A set of items whose labels are trusted enough to measure systems or judges against.
The versioned document that defines each label, with decision rules and worked examples, so that different annotators reach the same answer.
The tendency for evaluation criteria to change as people grade more outputs and discover what they actually care about.
How often independent annotators give the same label to the same items, used to judge whether a guideline is reproducible.
A measure of agreement between two annotators that subtracts the agreement expected by chance, from 1 for perfect agreement to 0 for chance level.
An agreement measure that works for any number of annotators, missing labels and ordered scales.
Resolving items on which annotators disagree by having a senior reviewer decide and record the reason.
The highest score a perfect system can reach on a test set because some of its gold labels are wrong.
The tendency of an annotator who sees a suggested label to accept it, which inflates agreement without improving reliability.
